aerial_color.description: The color distant ridges fade into away from the sun.

aerial_density.description: Aerial extinction per world unit at height zero; 0 turns it off.

aerial_falloff.description: How fast the air thins with height, per world unit.

aerial_glow.description:
How strongly distant ridges fade into a glow of the sun's color

aerial_start.description:
Aerial perspective begins this far from the camera (world
units): beyond it, air dims what lies behind it toward the light
it scatters. Unlike fog it is unbounded and spans kilometers.

ambient.description: Scale of the sky's ambient light on surfaces.

contrast.description:
Contrast around mid grey after tone mapping: the slope of an
S-curve that keeps black and white; 0 flattens, 1 keeps it, and
the curve is steepest at 1.5.

emission.description:
Scale of material emission: how strongly lamps, lit windows and
other artificial lights show in this light, dim by day and full
at night.

fog_density.description: Fog density per world unit at height zero.

fog_falloff.description: How fast fog thins with height, per world unit.

fog_start.description: Fog begins this far from the camera (world units).

ground.description:
Sky color below the horizon: downward surfaces take their
ambient light from it.

horizon.description:
Sky color at the horizon: vertical surfaces take their ambient
light from it.

preset.description: The preset the other fields override.

rim.description:
Silhouette light in the horizon color, facing away from the
camera.

saturation.description: Saturation after tone mapping; 1 keeps it.

shadow_tint.description:
Hue of dark tones after tone mapping (split toning), as a color
gain scaled to keep luminance; white, like black, keeps them.
Cool shadows against warm highlights read as vivid.

specular.description:
Scale of sun highlights and sky reflections; 1 is physically
based.

sun_direction.description:
Direction toward the sun; any nonzero length, normalized when
rendered.

vibrance.description:
Saturation added to muted colors more than to vivid ones; 0 adds
none.

zenith.description:
Sky color straight up: upward surfaces take their ambient light
from it.

AutoExposure.description:
Auto exposure: the eye adapting to the light in view. Each frame a
meter reads the frame drawn (a grid of samples, the middle of the view
counting more than its corners and the sky less than the rest) and
averages their light in stops, leaving out shares of the darkest and
the brightest. Later frames' exposure, eased quickly when the view
grows brighter and slowly when it grows darker, as eyes do, rises over
the atmosphere's authored exposure by two parts. The time of day's:
under the physically based sky, its own adaptation to its light (up to
4 stops), but at most `night` stops with the sun 14 degrees or more
below the horizon, easing there from 4 degrees below, so dusk dims as
before and night keeps dark. The view's: that average against what the
light falling on level ground gives an open view, beyond a stop either
way, so a cave by day brightens and a view of the bright sky darkens;
at night dark views stay dark. Opt-in.

brighten.description:
The most stops a dark view raises exposure, as a cave by day; none
at night, easing as the time of day's limit does.

center.description: How many times what the view's corners count the middle counts.

compensation.description:
Stops added to the exposure: positive brightens the view,
negative darkens it.

darken.description: The most stops a bright view lowers exposure.

night.description: The most stops the time of day raises exposure at night.

skip_bright.description: The share of the brightest samples it leaves out (the sun, lamps).

skip_dark.description: The share of the darkest samples the meter's average leaves out.

sky.description: How much the sky counts against what stands under it.

strength.description:
How far exposure follows the view: 0 not at all, 1 brings its
average all the way to within a stop of what its light gives an
open view.

to_brighter.description:
Seconds over which exposure goes most of the way (all but 1/e)
toward its new value after the view grows brighter.

to_darker.description: The same after the view grows darker.

StampOp.description:
What a stamp does where it reaches: raise or lower heights by meters,
level them toward a height, or cut holes in the terrain.

oneOf.description:
Cells whose centers lie within the radius are holes: no surface
draws or collides there.

BrowserControl.description:
Host controls available alongside read-only [`DevRequest`] operations.
The browser host enforces pause/lifecycle rules. Parsing validates
structure and the protocol version; the host also validates finite values,
ranges, and u64 revision parsing before changing state.

oneOf.description:
Preview fixed-tick poses at a chosen fraction without advancing clocks.
Requires pause; ordinary step/render/capture retain authoritative poses.

gpu.description:
Present through GPU blending/composition/culling
instead of the exact CPU path; for comparisons.

oneOf.description: Temporarily toggle visibility culling and render without advancing clocks.

Temporarily replace environment sections and render while paused.
Sections are a scene `environment`'s, validated alike; omitted
sections stay. A scene with an environment restores its own on
reload; persist a look by saving it there.

merge.description:
Whether a named section's omitted fields keep their current
values instead of taking their defaults.

oneOf.description:
Temporarily set terrain's level of detail and render while paused:
`subdivision_error` replaces the settings' pixels the drawn ground may
stray from its true surface, `pixel_error` the settings' pixels a level's
samples span where its tiles stream and shade, and `freeze` holds the
detail eye at the camera's current position while the camera moves on,
so every distance switch stays where it stood: terrain streaming, its
subdivision and shading levels, the ground's relief and displacement,
ground cover and its canopy, placed objects' thinning, kept shadow
windows and river water. Omitted fields stay as
they are. Terrain's leaves, normals, tiles and patches, materials, sky
visibility and detail show in the debug views (the environment's
`debug_view` section).

Temporarily edit a generated terrain over its layers and bakes
and render while paused: `change` raises or lowers the
ground by meters, levels it to a world height or cuts holes in it, at
full strength within `radius` meters of world `center` `[x, z]` and
fading over `falloff` more, under `id` (letters, digits, `_`, `-` and
`.`), which repeating leaves the terrain alone. Only the tiles
under it regenerate. Returns whether it applied, the edits standing,
where tiles regenerate (world `min` and `max` `[x, z]`) and the most
the ground moved (meters). `terrain` names a scene's terrain entity
(the first terrain when omitted). The `Terrain` inspector lists the
edits as stamp layers to save into the scene.

Take the terrain's last edit away and render while
paused; `terrain` as for `terrain_edit`.

Put back the last edit undo took away, unless an edit came since,
and render while paused.

Temporarily draw a river over a generated terrain, or take one away,
and render while paused: `points` (world `[x, z]`, from upstream, two
or more; the river runs along the smooth line through them) with
optional `width` (meters across its channel), `depth` (meters its
channel's middle lies below its banks) and `discharge` (cubic meters a
second its bankfull flood carries), each one value for the whole river
or one for each point, and an optional `name`, under `id` (letters,
digits, `_`, `-` and `.`); no points take away the river drawn under
`id`. Drawing the same river under an `id` again leaves the terrain
alone; another replaces it. What a river leaves out the terrain's
hydrology derives, as for its own rivers. The terrain bakes its
hydrology and what follows it again with every drawn river given just
before it, and only the tiles where its rivers or roads then differ
regenerate. Returns whether it applied, the rivers drawn, and where the
river drawn, replaced or taken away lies (world `min` and `max`
`[x, z]`). `terrain` names a scene's terrain entity (the first terrain
when omitted), which needs a hydrology layer. The `Terrain` inspector
lists the drawn rivers to save into the scene as a rivers layer before
its hydrology layer.

Press a track as a deformer would, now, and render
while paused: a capsule `radius` meters across from world `from`
`[x, z]` to `to` (a footprint at `from` when omitted), sinking ground
as deformable as that `depth` meters along its middle, round
(`flatness` 0) to flat (1). `clear`
forgets every track first. Not a source change: the log and the map
keep it until cleared or refilled. Returns the stamp, the stamps the
log holds and whether deformation is enabled.

Send navigation agent `entity` (authored ID) walking to world
`destination` `[x, z]`, or stop it with null, and
render while paused; steps then walk it. Not a source change.
Returns its status.

Set an authored entity's animation player and render while paused:
its clip (an animation ID of the scene), time in seconds, speed and
looping; omitted values stay. Returns them before and after.

Remove streamed items for good, or restore them, by
ID (`scene/root` for scenes), and render while
paused: `clear` restores every item first. Loaded cells despawn and
spawn them at once. Not a source change: WorldChanges keeps them,
as a game's save would. Returns how many items are removed.

Set a complete temporary world-space camera and render while paused.
Its values keep the rules of scenes' cameras (`SceneCamera`), the
field of view in radians.

RAF-paced host sampling, bounded to ten seconds; advances one tick per
sample in step mode and no gameplay in render/present modes. Present mode
samples existing fixed-tick history at alpha 0.5. Clears pending input.

Advance exactly `ticks` fixed ticks, then one presentation/render
boundary.

Run `count` ordinary frames `interval_ms` apart while paused, as play
runs them after a pause: the first advances no time, each later one
`interval_ms`, without input (pending input is cleared), presented
and antialiased as play's are; then stay paused. With `capture`,
the host captures the last frame as it was drawn, without drawing
again, as `capture` keeps its files.
Replace the temporary batch applied on the next explicit step.
Extract and render current state without advancing gameplay.

Render while paused and wait for presentation before host capture.
Omitted alpha renders authoritative current state; a supplied fraction
previews existing fixed-tick history without advancing gameplay.

gpu.description:
With `alpha`, capture GPU presentation instead of
the exact CPU path.

oneOf.description:
Runs the game's own control `name` with `args`, as the page
registers it (a Stress Lab workload, look or view), then renders.
The bridge's describe lists the game's controls.

args.description: The control's arguments, a JSON object.

oneOf.description: Fetch saved source and require both expected runtime and source revisions.

Panics the engine, as a bug in it would, to check what the host does
then: the engine stops for good, and every later request answers
`runtime_panicked` with the panic's message and where it happened.

Fails the renderer's lazily created feature `feature` as a GPU error
would: its next creation makes an invalid object, which its first
frame uses. The renderer disables it alone; then renders.

Loses the GPU device, as a driver reset or a removed GPU would, to
check what the host does then: the renderer fails for good, and the
first frame after, as every later one, fails `render_failed` with a
message naming the loss, which this control answers with.

Removes the mesh the scene's entity `entity` (its authored ID) draws
from the asset library, as a game unloading it would, and renders
while paused: every entity drawing that mesh then draws nothing,
which frame statistics' `missing_assets` counts and `assets` lists,
each entity with its position. Answers how many entities draw it.

What drew pixel (`x`, `y`) of the view (physical pixels from its top
left) and how it looks: renders a frame of the debug views' targets,
then a shaded one, as `capture` renders them (with `alpha` and `gpu`,
GPU-presented frames, which draw levels of detail and impostor
cards as play does), and reads both back at the pixel: what drew it,
its object and the entity that is, its level of detail, normal,
depth and world position, the sun shadow lookup deciding it, the
fragments covering it, and its shaded and displayed colors.

gpu.description:
With `alpha`, GPU-presented frames instead of the exact CPU
path.

Camera.description:
Right-handed Y-up perspective. Lens distances use world units; 0 < near <
far; FOV is in radians.

Clouds.description: The cloud layer. Opt-in: a scene without a `clouds` section has none.

base.description: The world height of its base, meters.

coverage.description: How much of the sky it covers: 0 clear, 1 overcast.

in_view.description:
Whether the view marches the clouds after the opaque scene: then
they stand in front of whatever lies beyond them, all around a camera
inside the layer and below one above it, and the dome shows them
behind every surface only while the camera is under the layer.

resolution.description:
The dome's texels around the horizon; a quarter as many from the
horizon up.

scale.description: The meters across its largest shapes.

shadows.description: How much of the sun's light its shadows take from the ground.

slices.description: The frames over which ordinary frames march the whole dome.

wind.description: The wind it drifts in, meters per second along x and z.

Clouds.title: SceneClouds

Collider.description:
Local cuboid/sphere, symmetric layer filters and sensor flag. Current
authoritative world admission and refreshed collision-cache status are
independent of visibility and interpolation.

cache_status.description:
Active/invalid in the refreshed cache; not_cached includes overflow;
unavailable means the plugin is absent.

world_valid.description: Admission of the current authoritative world transform, independent of visibility.

Collider.title: ColliderView

CollisionWorld.description:
Authoritative spatial cache refreshed for inspection without advancing
clocks or committing sensor events. Includes source frame/tick, cache
revision, completeness, invalid/overflow counts and query budgets. Memory
counts are cache payload, not process totals.

cache_bytes.description: Reserved collision cache payload; not total process memory.

placed_colliders.description: Placed objects colliding within terrains' collision radius.

revision.description: Cache revision and source clocks are decimal strings, not runtime handles.

CollisionWorld.title: CollisionWorldView

DebugViewMode.description: What a debug view shows each pixel as.

oneOf.description: The shaded image: no debug view.

What drew it, a color per kind: meshes gray-blue, placed objects
teal, impostor cards magenta, virtual geometry violet, terrain brown,
ground cover green, water blue, the sky pale blue.

Its level of detail, from the finest: red, orange, yellow, green,
cyan, blue, violet and gray, for meshes and placed objects (their own
mesh, then each simplification) and terrain's patches alike;
impostor cards magenta, virtual geometry a color per cluster. Frames
GPU presentation draws (`capture` with `alpha` and `gpu`) show levels
and cards as play does; exact frames draw every mesh whole.

Impostor cards magenta (cards fading over their meshes pink) over
everything else gray: where cards stand in for meshes.

Which sun shadow lookup decided it: the clipmap's levels green to
blue, from the finest, a terrain's horizon purple, where no level is
drawn gray; darker where it lies in shadow, black without sun
shadows.

How it casts sun shadows: meshes red, placed objects orange,
virtual geometry violet, impostor cards casting cards of their own
magenta, terrain brown, what casts none gray.

How many fragments passed the depth test there as the frame drew,
from dark blue (one) through green and yellow to white (ten or more).

Its shading normal, as colors: x red, y green, z blue, each from 0
(pointing back) to 1 (along the axis); terrain's its smooth
surface's.

Terrain's level-0 tiles and patches (sixteen samples a side): tile
edges red, patch edges dark, the ground between gray; everything else
as in `cards`.

Terrain's surface materials, each in its own color, blended in the
shares the ground shows them in.

The share of the sky terrain's ground sees, unlit, from black (none)
to white (all of it).

How terrain's ground shows its materials' maps: green where their
detail shows, filtered over the pixel, yellow as that filtering
averages their normal maps' slopes into roughness, red where a whole
repeat spans less than a pixel and their means stand in, blue where it
shows as its cover's canopy.

How deep terrains' water stands, tiles' and simulated alike, from
pale (none) through blue (half a meter) to navy (two meters or
more), on a square-root scale. The water's views draw water wherever
it lies, however little of the pixel it covers, and show the sea,
falls' sheets and everything else gray, the sky dark, all unlit.

How fast the water runs, from dark violet (still) through crimson to
yellow (six meters a second or more).

Its Froude number, its speed over its shallow waves' (√(g·depth)):
calm water from deep blue (0) to pale cyan, shooting water from
yellow to red (3 or more), water running at its waves' speed (1)
black.
How turbulent it runs, from dark teal (0) through green to lime (1).
Where white water is born, from dark blue (none) to white (1).

The reach of the stream it runs in, by the stream's slope: pools
blue, plane beds cyan, steps and pools green, cascades orange, falls
red; water no stream holds (lakes) violet.

The foam it carries, as its flow churns it up, carries it and loses
it (`engine_terrain::shallow_water`), from dark brown (none) through
sand to white (the most water carries).

How far across its water body is: a river's width, a lake's
equal-area diameter, on a logarithmic scale from violet (a quarter
meter) through teal (32 meters) to pale yellow (4096 meters or more).

Its eddies' turbulent Froude number: the speed they turn at,
(g·U·S·depth)^(1/3) for its speed U and its surface's slope S, over
√(g·depth); from dark (calm) through orange, where they start
breaking its surface white (`engine_terrain::BREAK_ONSET`), to white,
where they break it white all over (`engine_terrain::BREAK_FULL`).

The roughness its shading gives its surface, from black (0, a
mirror) through copper to white (1): calm water's, widened by the
slopes of the waves a pixel hides.

DebugView.description:
Debug view settings: what frames show each pixel as, for agents and
people finding out why a pixel looks as it does. Off by default; a
view draws with its own pipelines, created the first time it shows,
and leaves screen effects, decals, transparent surfaces and temporal
antialiasing out.

shade.description:
Whether its colors darken where surfaces turn from the sun, so
shapes read.

DebugView.title: SceneDebugView

SceneDecalBlend.description: How a decal combines with the surface it lies on.

oneOf.description: Covering by alpha, lit like any surface: paint, posters, markings.

Multiplying the surface's color, keeping its light: dirt, cracks,
stains and scorch marks.

Decal.description:
A decal on this entity as a scene's `decal` field: its material
projected down the entity's local y onto the opaque surfaces inside its unit
box, fading on surfaces turning away beyond `fade_degrees`.

material.description: The material's authored ID; None when no scene instance owns it.

material_alive.description: Whether the material is still resident.

Decal.title: DecalView

max_decals.description:
An optional budget of decals a frame draws; beyond it the decals
nearest the camera win. Omitted, every decal draws.

extent.description: The meters of ground the map around the camera spans.

max_stamps.description:
An optional budget of stamps the log keeps, the oldest dropping
beyond it.

persist.description:
Whether the log keeps the stamps the map moves away from, so tracks
are there when the camera returns.

refill.description:
The seconds tracks take to refill to about a third of their depth;
0 never.

resolution.description:
The map's texels along a side; renderers keep fewer where the
device's buffers cannot hold them.

rim.description: How high the ground rises beside a track for its depth.

Deformer.description:
Presses tracks into deformable ground as a scene's `deformer`
field: each fixed tick, while its entity's world position lies at most
`contact` meters above the terrain under it (or below it), it presses a
footprint from where it pressed the tick before. Put it where an object
meets the ground: a wheel's or a foot's lowest point.

contact.description: Meters above the terrain within which it presses.

depth.description:
Meters it sinks ground as deformable as that along its middle,
deeper by however far it lies below the ground.

flatness.description:
Its footprint's shape: 0 round, deepest along its middle like a
wheel's rut; 1 flat, a foot's or a plate's level floor.

radius.description: Meters across the footprint it presses.

Deformer.title: Deformer

Dither.description:
Dithering: every write of color into an 8-bit target (the canvas, the
screen effects' scene and temporal antialiasing's history) adds noise
of about one step of what the target stores, so smooth gradients such
as dusk skies, fog and dark interiors show no bands, and temporal
antialiasing's history settles on the color instead of stopping a few
steps short. The noise is fixed per pixel, and turns every frame under
temporal antialiasing, which averages it. Off by default.
Dither.title: SceneDither

DynamicResolution.description:
Dynamic resolution settings: whether display frames scale the size
they draw at, between the least and the most scale, so their GPU
time keeps within a budget. It goes by two timestamps a frame where
the device times its work, else by the time between frames; it lowers
the scale at once while frames run over the budget and raises it a
step at a time while they run under, in steps that keep temporal
antialiasing's history steady. Off unless a scene names it; hosts
turn it on for play in a window or a page, and keep it off for
offscreen captures and measured runs.

budget_ms.description:
Milliseconds of GPU time each frame keeps within; omitted, the
display's refresh interval where the host knows it, else a
sixtieth of a second.

enabled.description:
Whether display frames scale the size they draw at to keep within
the budget.

max_scale.description: The most scale frames draw at on each axis.

min_scale.description:
The least scale frames draw at on each axis, of the size the
resolution policy and the user's scale give: at most `max_scale`.

DynamicResolution.title: SceneDynamicResolution

Floating.description:
Rides the sea: each fixed tick the entity rises and falls with the sea's
surface under it and leans about its own heading. Unparented entities
only; nothing moves without an enabled sea.

draft.description: Meters of it below the surface.

tilt.description: How far it leans: 0 upright, 1 with the surface's normal.

Floating.title: SceneFloating

crown_depth.description:
Meters into a crown over which the sun's light halves: masked
leaves and needles, and the cards baked from them, take the sun
through their crown from its sun-facing side, down along the
sun and across from where the crown meets sunlit air, instead
of the first caster toward the sun shadowing them whole; 0
turns it off.

ground_blend.description:
Meters up from the ground over which plants' color and light
blend into the ground's at their base; 0 turns it off.

hashed_cutoff.description:
Whether masked leaves dissolve over their texture's coverage on
temporally antialiased frames, a threshold turning across pixels
and frames instead of the material's cutoff.

transmission.description:
Sunlight leaves, needles and blades pass toward the eye, seen
against the sun through them, tinted by their color and shaded
as the sun is; 0 turns it off.

variation.description:
How far each plant's leaves stray from its material's color, by
a hash of where it stands, along a gradient from drier to deeper
green; bark keeps its color. 0 turns it off.

Applied.description: Whether the frame applied an effect its settings ask for.

CellStats.description: World streaming's state after the last extraction.

pending.description: Cells within range still waiting to load.

rows.description:
Rows of the clouds' dome this frame marched: all of them on exact
frames, a slice on ordinary ones, none without clouds.

view_pixels.description:
Pixels of the view whose clouds this frame marched, a ray each: its
render size's, none without clouds or with their march in the view
off.

CullingStats.description: What GPU culling ran and left undrawn.

active.description:
Whether this GPU-presented display frame ran it, without an instance
budget (occlusion culling draws in two phases around its test).

instances.description:
Visible instances it left undrawn (occluded, or covering no pixel
center), read back with the visible count; `None` otherwise.

stamps.description: Stamps this frame pressed into the map around the camera.

texels.description:
The map's texels along a side: 0 while off, fewer than the settings'
where the device's buffers cannot hold them.

dropped_impostors.description:
Opaque draw groups that qualified for impostors but draw their meshes
because a budget or the GPU's texture array layers left them none.

impostor_instances.description: Instances drawn as impostors, read back like `lod0_instances`.

impostors.description:
Impostors resident: loaded from their records, or baked where no
pack or store held them.

lod0_instances.description:
GPU-culled frames with levels of detail: instances drawn as their
mesh, read back with the visible count; `None` otherwise.

lod1_instances.description:
Instances drawn as their mesh's first simplification, read back like
`lod0_instances`.

lod2_instances.description:
Instances drawn as their mesh's second simplification, read back like
`lod0_instances`.

meshes_without_levels.description:
Resident meshes that could have levels of detail drawing without:
no pack or store held the levels the cook makes
(`cargo xtask cook`).

Drawn.description: What a feature drew, and what a budget or the GPU's bindings left out.

dropped.description: Items a budget or the GPU's bindings left out.

invalid.description: Items breaking their rules, which no frame draws.

active.description:
Whether it scaled this frame: a display frame with dynamic resolution
on.

budget_ms.description: The milliseconds of GPU time frames keep within, while active.

scale.description:
The scale the frame drew at on each axis, of the size the resolution
policy and the user's scale give: 1 while inactive.

active.description: Whether this frame metered its exposure.

metered.description:
The meter's average of the light in view before exposure, in
hundredths of a stop (log2 of linear light), read back alike.

stops.description:
The exposure frames show, in hundredths of a stop above the
atmosphere's authored exposure (below it when negative), read back a
few frames late; 0 in frames not metering.

view.description:
How much brighter the view is than the light falling on level
ground gives an open view, in hundredths of a stop, read back alike:
negative in a cave by day.

blades.description: Blades the last read-back frame drew.

dropped.description: Blades past the capacity or budget, which dropped.

reach.description: Meters from the eye ground cover reached this frame, rounded.

tiers.description:
The most tiers it grew in: the first's, out to where blades span a
pixel, and doublings past it.

JobStats.description: Workers, their jobs and the host's output cache.

cache_hits.description:
Records the host's packs and store handed back instead of running
their jobs.

cache_mismatches.description: Verifying, records differing from a fresh run.

failed.description:
Jobs failed. A record fetched alone that no pack or store holds
([`MISSING_RECORD`]) is no failure: its owner makes it.

held.description:
Jobs the host's scheduler holds: on its workers, or looked up in its
packs and store. None once every job handed out ended, an earlier
engine's included.

in_place.description:
Jobs run in place: by a host without workers, or an engine no host
serves.

running.description: Jobs handed out and not done.

cluster_overflow.description:
Cluster entries beyond the clusters' budget or the storage still
growing, read back like `visible`.

dropped.description: Usable lights beyond the budget or without a valid pose.

invalid.description: Lights breaking their rules, which no frame draws.

shaded.description: Local lights the frame shaded within the budget.

visible.description:
Lights that reached a view cluster, read back a few frames late;
`None` before the first read-back or without lights.

NavStats.description:
What navigation did at the last fixed tick: agents, and
those searching (and of them those waiting for records or their
terrain's bakes), walking, arrived and unable to reach their
destination; the samples of search work the tick did; and the tiles'
grounds and portals held for walks.

grounds.description: Tiles whose ground navigation holds for walks.

portals.description: Tiles whose portals of a walk graph navigation holds.

searching.description: Agents whose walk is being searched.

unreachable.description: Agents whose destination no walk reaches.

waiting.description:
Agents whose search waits for records the host has yet to hand
back, or for its terrain's bakes.

work.description: Samples of search work the tick did.

OccupancyStats.description: The occupancy maps around the detail eye.

averages.description:
Times a map took the mean of the finer one inside it where that one
changed.

redraws.description:
Times a map redrew cells: each follows the detail eye in steps and
redraws where objects change.

PhysicsStats.description: Physics at the last fixed tick, read when the stats are.

awake.description: Of them, awake: moving, or pushed this tick.

contacts.description: Contacts touching between bodies and solids or each other.

held.description:
Of them, held still where the world's solids under them are not
resident yet.

solids.description:
The world's solids the solver holds for bodies to meet: terrain
tiles, placed objects and colliders near them.

water_samples.description: Samples of the world's water the tick's bodies took.

dropped.description: Probes a budget or the GPU's texture array layers left out.

ready.description: Probes surfaces could reflect this frame.

ResolutionStats.description:
The frame's sizes: the display's, which the surface or canvas and every
screen-sized target take, and the one it drew at from their top-left
corner, which its last pass upscaled to the display.

display_height.description: The display's height in physical pixels.

display_width.description:
The display's width in physical pixels: the host's whole view, unless
the device's largest texture holds less, which the display then fits
within at its aspect.

dropped_pixels.description:
Pixels of the view the host asked for that the device's largest
texture left out of the display.

gpu_ms.description:
Milliseconds the GPU took over the last frame it timed, from two
timestamps around its work, read back a few frames late; `None`
where the device times no work.

render_height.description: The height the frame drew at in physical pixels.

render_width.description:
The width the frame drew at in physical pixels: the resolution
policy's for the view at the user's scale, within the display, times
dynamic resolution's scale; the display's own for debug views and
exact frames.

active.description: Whether the sun cast shadows this frame.

casters.description:
Casters the redrawn tiles drew, read back a few frames late; `None`
before the first read-back.

draws.description:
Indexed draws into the clipmap's tiles, beside the camera pass's
`draw_calls`.

moving_casters.description:
Moving casters' draws into the tiles they cross, read back like
`casters`.

moving_left_out.description:
Moving casters' draws into tiles they cross that their draw groups'
room left out, read back like `casters`.

moving_tiles.description: Tiles moving casters drew over this frame.

sky_drawn.description:
Sky occlusion's maps this frame drew: one at most, while the camera
strays from them or their still meshes change.

sky_maps.description:
Sky occlusion's maps of still meshes seen from the sky
(`sky_occlusion`), drawn around the camera: two per direction in use
at most, and until a direction's are drawn it counts as open sky.

tiles_marked.description:
Tiles the pixels read back latest read, at the levels their size on
screen picks: those the clipmap draws.

tiles_missing.description:
Tiles pixels read that hold no drawn slot yet, for want of slots or
of the redraw budget: lookups read a coarser level there.

tiles_reclaimed.description: Kept tiles whose slots this frame gave to tiles pixels read.

tiles_resident.description:
Tiles holding a slot of the atlas: those pixels read and those kept
from before while slots last.

SkyStats.description: The physically based sky, and the exposure frames show.

exposure.description: Auto exposure's meter, which replaces the sky's own adaptation.

tables.description:
Tables this frame uploaded or built: two when its air's tables
arrived, one more when the sun, the camera's height or the air
changed; none without the sky.

dropped.description:
Terrains whose bounce light the horizon maps' layers or the probes'
buffers could not hold this frame, which take none.

levels.description:
The most levels of probes a terrain's bounce light relit this frame:
those whose reach meets the terrain, the coarsest always.

probes.description:
The probes bounce light relit this frame, over every level around
the detail eye.

relit.description:
Terrains whose bounce light relit this frame: every frame, however
the sun and sky stand.

dropped_materials.description:
Surface materials past the palette's capacity, or whose maps the
shared arrays cannot hold (block compressed, or sized unlike the first
material's), which show a plain color instead.

dropped_placed_objects.description:
Placed objects the device's storage bindings left out: those past
what the objects' buffers hold, and entries past what the views'
lists hold, once each view and level leaving them out, read back a
few frames late.

dropped_tiles.description: Tiles the tile budget or the device's texture array layers dropped.

fallback_tiles.description:
Tiles the camera's view draws and shows that are not resident yet,
whose ground coarser tiles stand in for.

gpu_controls.description: Tiles the GPU gave control values this frame.

horizons.description: Terrains casting long sun shadows through horizon maps.

leaves.description:
Leaves of the terrains' subdivisions the camera drew, as read back a
few frames later.

lighting_uploads.description:
Maps of terrains' lighting this frame uploaded, as it arrived or
changed: sky and horizon maps, one each per terrain. The sun moving
uploads none.

macro_maps.description:
Terrains whose macro color maps are here: the tint and growth their
bakes give their ground.

placed_far_objects.description:
Of those, objects standing far away, which hide where the tiles
holding them instead are resident.

placed_impostors.description:
Placed objects' impostors resident, which the camera draws far away
and shadow maps cast as cards; counted in `level_of_detail.impostors`
too.

placed_objects.description:
Objects placement layers stand on resident level-0 tiles, each culled
on the GPU every frame.

refused_splits.description:
Splits the subdivisions refused for want of room for their leaves
(`TerrainSettings::subdivision_leaves`), as read back: the ground
there stays coarser.

shadow_patches.description: Patches the shadow clipmap's regions drew of the ground.

shallow_subdivisions.description:
Terrains whose subdivision the device's storage bindings keep
shallower than `TerrainSettings::subdivision_depth` asks.

sky_maps.description: Terrains whose sky visibility maps are here.

white_water.description:
Emitters of spray and mist white water spawned at terrains' rapids,
where their settled water loses energy fastest.

VirtualGeometryStats.description: Virtual geometry, read back a few frames late.

dropped.description: Cluster selections dropped while their storage grew.

dropped_pages.description:
Wanted pages (with arrivals since) that found no room under the
budget or the device's limits.

failed_pages.description:
Page reads that failed or held no valid page since streaming
started, each read again later; the renderer's
`latest_page_failure` says why the latest did.

missing_pages.description:
Pages the last read-back frame wanted and lacked: 0 once its view had
all the detail it asked for.

occluded_clusters.description: The camera's clusters occlusion culling left undrawn.

visibility_buffer.description:
Whether the visibility buffer resolved the camera's virtual geometry
rather than drawing it forward.

WaterStats.description: Terrains' water, as their tiles hold it.

blocks.description: Blocks of tiles' water resident on the GPU, a patch's each.

dropped_blocks.description:
Blocks this frame dropped for want of the device's texture array
layers, whose water does not draw.

dropped_touches.description:
Solids standing in that square past the most its water takes, which
push none of it.

leaves.description:
Leaves of terrains' water's subdivisions the last read-back frame
drew, a few frames late.

refused.description:
Splits terrains' water's subdivisions refused for want of room for
their leaves (`Water::subdivision_leaves`), as read back a few frames
late: the water there stays coarser.

simulated_cells.description:
Cells along a side of the square around the camera over which
rivers run live: 0 while none do, fewer than the water settings ask
where the device's storage bindings cannot hold its buffers.

touches.description:
Solids standing in that square whose push its water takes this
frame, nearest the eye first: bodies and colliders, at most
`SIM_TOUCHES`.

CPU observations from the last submitted frame and the renderer's report
of it. Render time is not GPU time.

culled_instances.description: Valid instances culling proved outside the view.

disabled_features.description:
The renderer's features it disabled for good, by name: one whose
creation failed validation, or that an uncaptured GPU error named
by its objects' labels. Frames render without them.

draw_calls.description:
Draw commands of the camera's mesh passes, each counted once however
many occlusion phases issue it: each opaque mesh group's, one per
level of detail on GPU-presented frames, the impostors', virtual
geometry's forward bins and the transparent groups'. `shadows.draws`
counts the shadow maps'.

dropped_instances.description: Visible instances the instance budget left undrawn.

dropped_seconds.description: Total simulation time discarded by the fixed-step budget in this session.

dynamic_resolution.description: Dynamic resolution's scale of the size frames draw at.

extraction_ms.description: Milliseconds the frame spent extracting the render snapshot.

fixed_steps.description: Fixed simulation ticks this frame ran.

frame.description: The frame these stats describe, as `FrameTime::frame` counts it.

haze.description: The haze's march: the sunlight the near air scatters.

instances.description:
Number of mesh instances submitted (before GPU clipping). GPU-culled
frames report the read-back visible count limited by the instance
budget, or the budgeted candidate count before any read-back.

invalid_transforms.description:
Renderable entities skipped because their derived transform is
invalid.

jobs.description: The host's workers and their jobs, read when the stats are.

loading.description:
Whether terrains have yet to load the camera's view whole, or a
record game code's content waits for (its generated meshes and
textures), a static table the scene wants or its pipeline list has
yet to arrive, read when the stats are: hosts keep preparing
meanwhile.

mesh_upload_bytes.description: Vertex/index bytes initialized for meshes first seen this frame.

missing_assets.description:
Renderable entities skipped because a mesh, material, or texture is
absent.

navigation.description: Navigation agents at the last fixed tick, read when the stats are.

physics.description: Rigid bodies at the last fixed tick, read when the stats are.

pipelines_compiling.description:
Whether the GPU may still be compiling pipelines earlier frames
created, read when the stats are.

pipelines_created.description:
Pipelines this frame created: 0 once everything the scene draws is
compiled.

pipelines_listed.description:
Pipelines the scene's pipeline list created up front, while the
session prepared.

pipelines_unlisted.description:
Pipelines the session created that the scene's pipeline list
lacked, once it arrived: 0 while the list holds every pipeline the
session draws with.

read_back_age.description:
GPU-culled frames only: how many GPU-presented frames late the counts
read back with the visible count (`instances`, `triangles`,
`occlusion_culling`, `subpixel_culling` and `level_of_detail`'s
instances) are, 1 when they arrived as soon as they could, more while
the GPU falls behind; `None` before the first read-back. A check that
changed what they count presents until this is below the frames it
presented since.

render_candidates.description: Every entity carrying a mesh, before transform and asset checks.

render_ms.description: Milliseconds the frame spent preparing and submitting GPU work.

render_passes.description: The passes this frame ran, in order.

resident_mesh_bytes.description: Vertex/index bytes retained on the GPU after this frame.

resident_meshes.description: Number of distinct meshes retained on the GPU.

resident_texture_bytes.description: Asset texel bytes retained on the GPU after this frame.

resident_textures.description: Number of asset textures retained on the GPU, excluding renderer white.

resolution.description: The display's size and the size the frame drew at.

simulation_ms.description: Milliseconds the frame spent in fixed and variable simulation.

sky.description: The physically based sky, and the exposure frames show.

texture_upload_bytes.description: Texel bytes uploaded for textures first seen this frame.

tick.description:
The last fixed tick that frame completed, as `FixedTime::tick`
counts it.

triangles.description:
Triangles the camera's mesh draws submitted, at their levels of
detail and impostors' two each: exact on CPU-prepared frames, read
back with the visible count on GPU-culled ones. Virtual geometry

upload_bytes.description:
Actual bytes uploaded or initialized: changed camera/instances and new
assets. An unchanged rendered frame can submit draws with zero upload
bytes. Excludes renderer startup resources such as the four-byte white
texture.

visible_instances.description:
Valid instances surviving culling, before the instance budget;
GPU-culled frames report the latest read-back count.
